title: My Q1 gamedev used at least ~30% less energy with AI than without
author: bitbutter
selftext:
tldr; in my case, the same work would have cost more energy if i'd completed it without llms. Method and more detail here:  
[https://georgeoughttohelp.com/the-energy-efficiency-case-for-llm-use/](https://georgeoughttohelp.com/the-energy-efficiency-case-for-llm-use/)

comments.author: sumane12
comments.body: Oh no, the anti's are going to be so mad thatAI actually REDUCED energy consumption lol.

comments.author: lesuperhun
comments.body:
the main issue with that :   
the other data is projected data. ie : estimated value based on the assumption the project would have taken a hundred/two hundred more days without ai. not actual value.

sadly, given that value is complete guesswork, the data extrapolated with that doesn't really hold any water.

replies.author: bitbutter
replies.body: the duration estimates are predictions based on 20 years of doing similar work. 'complete guesswork' is not accurate.

replies.author: hyrumwhite
replies.body: There’s too many variables here for this to have any real meaning

replies.author: GreatBigJerk
replies.body: Okay, where is the 20 years of historical data to back it up?

replies.author: bitbutter
replies.body:
lol  
  
look: facemaker is historical data: same project, known original duration, measured AI duration. & Axe Ghost gives me a baseline for the prototype estimate.  
  
the piece is a personal case study, adjust expectations accordingly.

replies.author: lesuperhun
replies.body:
except : it isn't the same project.

he already made it, so he knows the pitfalls of it. he knows what the project is supposed to be.

Coding has always been a minor part of developing. the hard part, the time consuming part has always been designing something that will be able to be coded well.

and, in twenty years, he likely learned a few things.

replies.author: bitbutter
replies.body:
"he already made it,"

he is me. and i address this already:

\> If I had reimplemented it by hand, with everything I learned the first time, I might have been done in three weeks.

replies.author: lesuperhun
replies.body:
let me rephrase then :

it isn't the same project, exactly because it is the same :

you didn't have to actually do most of the process, because it was already done.

and, if, given comparable constraints, you could have done it in three weeks, then, the true "comparable" value, would have been three weeks, not 173 workdays.

replies.author: bitbutter
replies.body:
where are you getting “173 workdays” from? i \*am\* comparing the FaceMaker rebuild with the three-week estimate.

the 8–10 month estimate is for the whole Q1 body of work, not for FaceMaker. the FaceMaker comparison in the article is specifically: two AI-assisted days versus maybe three weeks by hand, given what I had already learned the first time.

replies.author: bitbutter
replies.body: read the my post again man. I don't have the patience to spoon feed you this.

comments.author: notsofst
comments.body:
Your experience matches mine, I feel like it's an easy 2x-3x productivity improvement and that might be understating it.

Also understated is the fact that bringing your ideas to life faster is less discouraging and makes it more likely for projects to progress.

Get to market faster, better vibes, less effort.

I also have multiple decades of experience, though, which really helps wrangling the agents. However, the agents are already more effective than pretty much any offshore or contract team I've ever used.

replies.author: bitbutter
replies.body: yes. exactly the same thing for me.
